question.text: Mr. Vikram Rao runs a family office with INR 200 crore. He wants (a) daily liquidity on 60% of the corpus, (b) discretionary customised equity management on 25%, and (c) exposure to unlisted late-stage growth companies on 15%. Per NISM Ch 2.4, which combination of investment channels is MOST appropriate?

answer.text: (a) Fixed Deposit, (b) Mutual Fund, (c) Stock Broker
(a) Category III AIF, (b) Mutual Fund, (c) Specialized Investment Fund
(a) Mutual Fund / ETF, (b) Portfolio Management Services, (c) Category II AIF (PE Fund)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 2.4, daily liquidity and diversified listed exposure is best served by an open-ended Mutual Fund or ETF (traditional managed-portfolio vehicles also include ETFs). Discretionary customised management for HNIs is delivered by PMS, and unlisted late-stage growth fits a Cat II AIF Private Equity fund. This aligns each objective with the channel whose regulatory and structural design fits it. The Trap: Option A over-uses AIF for a need (daily liquidity) that AIF structurally cannot provide. Option B uses Fixed Deposit and Stock Broker, neither of which is a managed-portfolio channel for the stated objectives. Option C misplaces Category III AIF for daily liquidity and uses Mutual Fund where customised discretionary management is required, while also misusing SIF for unlisted late-stage growth. Note: Map each client objective to the channel whose structure fits — liquidity to MF/ETF, customised discretionary equity to PMS, and unlisted growth to a Category II PE AIF.
